channel.title: Case tracker — Custos
channel.description: Status changes and hearing updates on Indian technology-law cases tracked by Adv. Ashwani Kumar.

item.title: LiveLaw v. Union of India | Notice issued on challenge to automated blocking
item.description: On 19 November, a Delhi High Court Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice to the Union of India and Meta on LiveLaw's petition challenging Rule 4(4) of the IT Rules,…
item.content:encoded:
On 19 November, a Delhi High Court Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice to the Union of India and Meta on LiveLaw's petition challenging Rule 4(4) of the IT Rules, 2021, which requires large platforms to use automated tools to restrict content exactly identical to content already removed.

LiveLaw says three Instagram reels reporting Supreme Court hearings were restricted in India, two within about 15 minutes of posting, without any order, notice or reasons. The Additional Solicitor General suggested treating the petition as a representation and passing a reasoned order; LiveLaw's counsel called that a mere formality.

The Union and Meta have four weeks to file replies. Interim relief was not pressed. The matter is listed next on 18 January 2027, and similar challenges on 9 February 2027.

item.title: DPDP Act and RTI challenge | Hearing adjourned to 9 December
item.description: On 17 November, the Supreme Court listed the challenge to the DPDP Act's amendment of the RTI Act together with the connected petitions, including the Digital News Publishers Association's. The matter could not be taken…
item.content:encoded:
On 17 November, the Supreme Court listed the challenge to the DPDP Act's amendment of the RTI Act together with the connected petitions, including the Digital News Publishers Association's. The matter could not be taken up and was adjourned to 9 December.

On 27 October, the Court had issued notice on the news publishers' petition and declined an interim stay without hearing the Union. The RTI petitions were referred to a larger bench in February 2026.

item.title: Rekha Gupta v. AAP | Six URLs to be taken down in interim order
item.description: On 6 November, the Delhi High Court directed that six URLs carrying the AI-generated videos and images complained of be taken down, in an interim order in Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta's suit against the Aam Aadmi…
item.content:encoded:
On 6 November, the Delhi High Court directed that six URLs carrying the AI-generated videos and images complained of be taken down, in an interim order in Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta's suit against the Aam Aadmi Party.

The Court issued summons. The defendants are yet to be heard. The suit is listed next on 4 December.

item.title: Jangaon AI-drafted order | High Court suspends Collector's order said to rely on AI
item.description: On 3 November, Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court suspended the Jangaon Collector's order of 8 September in a land dispute. The petitioner says the order was passed ex parte, with AI tools and…
item.content:encoded:
On 3 November, Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court suspended the Jangaon Collector's order of 8 September in a land dispute. The petitioner says the order was passed ex parte, with AI tools and without verifying the facts.

The Court issued notice to the Revenue Principal Secretary, the Collector and the Tahsildar, and asked the Advocate-General what action is proposed. The matter was listed on 18 November; the outcome has not been reported yet.

item.title: Digital arrest scams | Banks must compensate victims where due diligence fails
item.description: On 29 October, a Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said the RBI's proposed anti-cyber-fraud regulations must require financial institutions to compensate victims where a fraud…
item.content:encoded:
On 29 October, a Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said the RBI's proposed anti-cyber-fraud regulations must require financial institutions to compensate victims where a fraud results from a failure of due diligence. The compensation must be at least equal to the customer's loss.

The Court said it would examine the draft regulations before they are notified. The RBI proposed notifying them by 30 November and bringing them into operation by 31 December.

The Court directed WhatsApp and other intermediaries to set out the measures they propose to prevent digital arrest scams, and to share them at the same time with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). Counsel for WhatsApp said the platform had acted against about 9,400 accounts.

The RBI was directed to file a list of all authorised financial institutions, and law enforcement agencies to report the status of digital arrest FIRs. The order was uploaded on 7 November, and the case was listed next on 23 November.

item.title: Kent RO v. Amazon | Summons issued; no interim relief yet
item.description: On 16 October, Justice Tejas Karia of the Delhi High Court issued summons in Kent RO Systems' suit against Amazon over the use of KENT as a sponsored-ads keyword, and on Kent's application for an ad interim injunction.…
item.content:encoded:
On 16 October, Justice Tejas Karia of the Delhi High Court issued summons in Kent RO Systems' suit against Amazon over the use of KENT as a sponsored-ads keyword, and on Kent's application for an ad interim injunction. Amazon accepted notice.

No interim relief has been granted. Amazon's reply to the application is due within three weeks and its written statement within 30 days. The application is listed next on 8 December.

item.title: Challenge to the DPDP Act and the RTI amendment: update
item.description:
Venkatesh Nayak v. Union of India (W.P.(C) 177/2026) and connected petitions, including the Digital News Publishers Association (Supreme Court)

The question: Whether s. 44(3), which narrowed the RTI exemption for personal information, and other provisions (ss. 17, 33, 36 and the Board's selection rules) are constitutional, and whether journalism needs an exemption.

Where it stands: Notice issued and no interim stay. The RTI petitions were referred to a larger bench in February 2026. On 27 October the Court issued notice on the news publishers' petition and declined an interim stay without hearing the Union. The matter was listed with the connected petitions on 17 November but could not be taken up, and was adjourned to 9 December.

Next listed 2026-12-09

item.title: Digital arrest scams and bank liability: update
item.description:
In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents (suo motu) (Supreme Court)

The question: What banks, the RBI and platforms such as WhatsApp must do to prevent digital arrest frauds, and who compensates victims.

Where it stands: On 29 October the Court said the RBI's new rules must make banks compensate victims where a failure of due diligence enabled the fraud, and that it would examine the draft rules before they are notified. It also asked WhatsApp to propose measures. The order was uploaded on 7 November. The case was listed again on 23 November; the outcome has not been reported yet.

Next listed 2026-11-23

item.title: AI deepfakes and political satire: update
item.description:
Smt. Rekha Gupta v. Aam Aadmi Party & Ors. (CS(OS) 1019/2026) (Delhi High Court)

The question: Whether AI-generated videos and images of the Delhi Chief Minister posted by a political party are protected satire or defamation.

Where it stands: Interim order of 6 November: six URLs directed to be taken down. Summons issued; the defendants are yet to be heard.

Next listed 2026-12-04

item.title: AI training and copyright: ANI's appeal: update
item.description:
ANI Media Pvt. Ltd. v. OpenAI (appeal against the order of 24 July 2026 in CS(COMM) 1028/2024) (Delhi High Court (Division Bench))

The question: Whether training ChatGPT on ANI's news content is fair dealing for research under s. 52 of the Copyright Act.

Where it stands: The single judge refused ANI an interim injunction on 24 July 2026. A Division Bench issued notice on ANI's appeal on 15 September and gave no interim direction. It is listed in early December; reports give 5 or 8 December.

Next listed 2026-12-05

item.title: Brand names sold as advertising keywords on Amazon: update
item.description:
Kent RO Systems Ltd. v. Amazon Seller Services Pvt. Ltd. (CS(COMM) 1145/2026) (Delhi High Court)

The question: Whether Amazon infringes the well-known mark KENT by letting sellers bid on it as a keyword in its sponsored-products ads, and whether Amazon can claim intermediary safe harbour.

Where it stands: On 16 October Justice Tejas Karia issued summons on Kent's application for an ad interim injunction; Amazon accepted notice. No interim relief has been granted. Amazon's reply is due within three weeks and its written statement within 30 days.

Next listed 2026-12-08

item.title: Children's safety online: update
item.description:
Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish (Supreme Court)

The question: How to protect children from online sexual exploitation without banning them from the internet.

Where it stands: Order of 15 October 2026: internet access is a fundamental right for children too; blanket age-based bans are disproportionate. The Court directed a child mode, a national hash database, faster takedowns and fines scaled to platform size. The Centre must report progress at the next hearing.

Next listed 2026-12-10

item.title: Collector's order allegedly drafted with AI: update
item.description:
Medipalli Komuraiah v. State of Telangana (writ petition) (Telangana High Court)

The question: Whether a revenue order in a land dispute, allegedly passed ex parte with AI tools and without verifying facts, can stand.

Where it stands: On 3 November Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar suspended the Jangaon Collector's order of 8 September, issued notice to the Revenue Principal Secretary, the Collector and the Tahsildar, and asked the Advocate-General what action is proposed. Listed on 18 November; the outcome has not been reported yet.

Listed 18 Nov 2026; next date awaited

item.title: Automated blocking of news reports (Rule 4(4), IT Rules): update
item.description:
Live Law Media Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors. (Delhi High Court)

The question: Whether the mandatory automated filtering duty in Rule 4(4) of the IT Rules, 2021 (as amended in February 2026) can be used to restrict news and court reporting without an order, notice or reasons to the publisher.

Where it stands: LiveLaw's Instagram reels reporting Supreme Court hearings were restricted in India, two of them within about 15 minutes of posting. On 19 November 2026 a Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice to the Union and Meta, with four weeks to reply. Interim relief was not pressed.

Next listed 2027-01-18

item.title: Facial recognition at protest sites: update
item.description:
SFLC.in v. Union of India; A.A. Rahim v. Union of India (Supreme Court)

The question: Whether police may use facial recognition on people at designated protest sites without a law authorising it.

Where it stands: Notice issued on 3 November 2026 on SFLC.in's petition, tagged with A.A. Rahim's earlier plea on the July Jantar Mantar protests. The Union is yet to reply.

Next date not yet reported

item.title: Ban on online money games: update
item.description:
Head Digital Works v. Union of India and connected cases (Supreme Court)

The question: Whether Parliament can ban all online money games, including games of skill, under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025.

Where it stands: On 5 August 2026 a bench led by the Chief Justice agreed to a final hearing. There is no interim stay, so the Act (in force since 1 May 2026) applies.

Final hearing date not yet announced

item.title: Meta's California clause v. Indian courts: update
item.description:
Meta Platforms v. Blink Digital (Bombay High Court)

The question: Whether an Indian advertiser's suit over disabled ad accounts must go to California under Meta's terms.

Where it stands: On 27 October the court refused Meta's application: claims under the IT Act and IT Rules need an Indian forum. The suit for restoration and damages continues; jurisdiction can still be argued at trial.

Suit continues

item.title: Data Protection Board appointments: update
item.description:
Not a case: the regulator under the DPDP Act (Union Government)

The question: When the Data Protection Board's Chairperson and Members will be appointed.

Where it stands: The Board was established in law on 13 November 2025, but no Chairperson or Member had been appointed as of mid-November 2026, even as consent manager registration opened on 13 November. The Kerala High Court recorded on 7 October that the Board was not functional.

Next listed 2027-05-13

item.title: No writ against Meta for blocking an account: update
item.description:
Sarthak Bhagat v. Union of India (Delhi High Court)

The question: Can a user challenge Instagram's account block by writ?

Where it stands: 27 October 2026: writ not maintainable against Meta; restoration must be sought by civil suit. The Grievance Appellate Committee was directed to decide the appeal quickly.

Decided 2026-10-27

item.title: User must get a copy of a takedown notice: update
item.description:
Haryana 24 News Network v. Union of India (Punjab & Haryana High Court)

The question: Was an SP's s. 79(3)(b) notice that got a news page blocked valid?

Where it stands: Reported 20 October 2026: the notice was without jurisdiction (Rule 3(1)(d) needs a DIG-rank officer), a copy must go to the user, and the page was ordered restored.

Decided 2026-10-20

item.title: Platforms can act on copyright complaints: update
item.description:
Anmol Jain v. Union of India (Madhya Pradesh High Court)

The question: Can Instagram suspend a creator's account over copyright complaints without a court order?

Where it stands: 17 September 2026: challenge to Rule 3(1)(b)(iv) dismissed; the grievance officer and GAC are adequate safeguards.

Decided 2026-09-17

item.title: Customs penalty built on fake AI citations set aside: update
item.description:
Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya v. Union of India (Supreme Court)

The question: Can an adjudication relying on non-existent cases stand?

Where it stands: 2 September 2026: ₹425 crore penalty set aside and sent back to a different officer; "assistance can never be substituted for adjudication."

Decided 2026-09-02

item.title: Fake citations make a decision "no decision at all": update
item.description:
Pooja Ramesh Singh v. J&K Bank Ltd., 2026 INSC 668 (Supreme Court)

The question: Effect of NCLT and NCLAT orders relying on non-existent judgments.

Where it stands: 2 July 2026: both orders set aside; citing AI-generated precedents without verification is professional misconduct; the BCI to frame guidelines.

Decided 2026-07-02
